selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts, aligning directly with the advertiser's health-tracking and fitness subcategories. Her low price sensitivity and preference for science-backed messaging match the app's mid-tier price point and science_backed core value.

The Fitness Enthusiast works out frequently and buys fitness services and recovery products, making them an ideal target for an AI-powered fitness and health app. Their appreciation for performance-oriented tools connects seamlessly to the app's tracking and metric optimization features.

The Convenience-First Millennial is a heavy subscription user who values speed and frictionlessness, directly matching the advertiser's subscription business model and convenience value. Their urban, mid-to-high income profile fits the target demographic for digital health applications found on publishers like Daily Form and Studiogrid.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent focuses on household, kids' products, and meal kits, which do not align with the core wellness_services and health_tracking focus of the advertiser.

The Gen Z Aesthete focuses on beauty, fashion, and functional beverages discovered via TikTok and Instagram, whereas the advertiser's app targets a slightly older demographic (25-55) seeking clinical, science-backed health metrics.
The Pet Parent is centered on pet food, pet supplies, and veterinary care, which has no logical intersection with a human health and fitness tracking application.
The Affluent Classic skews toward older demographics (50-68) focused on classic apparel and home goods rather than mobile app-based health tracking and telehealth services.
The Sustainability Buyer focuses on ethical supply chains and clean beauty rather than personal fitness metrics, testing, and AI health monitoring.
The Value-Conscious Shopper looks for discount-forward messaging, bundles, and bargain grocery or apparel options, which misaligns with the app's mid-tier subscription pricing model.
The Gifter is explicitly disinterested in subscription-only models, making them incompatible with the advertiser's primary subscription business model.
